doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Radio jazz as a kid and hearing the Fallacious Five
summary: He had only played marching and fireman's bands, loved Eddie Condon broadcasts on radio, and as a freshman heard John Fell and Jim Collier jamming in a dorm.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You played drums when you came here?

Not jazz. I played in the fireman’s band and the high school bands and the marching bands. But it wasn’t until I came here that I played jazz. I loved jazz but it was always listening to recordings. I used to listen to Ted Husing on Saturday mornings, the old famous sportscaster.

H-U-S-I-N-G. He lost his sight and he continued to broadcast on the radio. And he was a great lover of Eddie Condon and so I used to listen Saturday mornings when I was a kid in my mother’s car to Ted Husings’ broadcast of Eddie Condon, Wild Bill Davison, Cutty Cutshall. And I used to get so excited by that music I wanted to roll myself up into a ball and shove myself into the radio in the dashboard of the car. I just loved it. And when I came to Hamilton I already was predisposed to Dixieland and I walked, as a freshman, across the Quadrangle and I heard some jazz coming out of one window. I think it was the Carnegie dorm. John Fell was the clarinetist in the Fallacious Five. He was playing and Jim Collier was with him, the trombone player.
Oh and the author, the future author.
Yeah. And he’s the present member of my Gotham Jazz men in Manhattan. I recruited him to play trombone with us.
